input.quote: IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7.0 (Materials) is the only ownership/licence architecture in this hosting agreement. IBM correctly retains ownership of its pre-existing and generic Type II Materials, and Customer takes ownership of Type I Materials, so the walk-away (assignment of Customer IP) is not triggered. But the deliverable licence fails the fallback on material terms: the Type II licence is not perpetual, is confined to Customer's Enterprise only, and omits any right to modify or sublicense, so we could not adapt or share delivered reports, programs and documentation for our business. Separately, § 14.18 gives IBM and its Enterprise a standing right to store and use Customer contact information "anywhere they do business", to pass it to contractors, Business Partners and assignees for their "collective business activities" including promotions and marketing research - independent exploitation of Customer data well beyond processing to provide the Services. The redline makes the Type II licence perpetual, royalty-free and modifiable/sublicensable for our business, and confines IBM's rights in our Content, Customer Components and other Customer data to processing solely to provide the Services. We have not disturbed IBM's ownership of Type II Materials, the revocable Base Components platform licence in § 12.1 (its own hosting platform), or the Type I licence-back in § 7(b), none of which the selected checklist reaches.

proposal.summary: Broaden the Type II Materials licence to a perpetual, royalty-free right to use, modify, distribute and sublicense for Customer's business, and limit IBM's rights in Customer data to providing the Services.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We accept IBM's ownership of its pre-existing Type II Materials, but our fallback position requires a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense delivered Materials for our business, rather than an Enterprise-only, no-modification licence. We also limit IBM's rights in our Content and other Customer data (including contact information) to processing solely to provide the Services, instead of IBM's general business, promotional and marketing-research uses.
